title: Finite Q3 all-bond support-local weight recurrence stress test
question: Does a support-local energy weight give a stable two-orientation all-bond recurrence on the exact finite Q3 graph, and does one-layer support enlargement supply the missing critical topology input?
method: Construct the exact cube graph with twelve bonds, a square-face subvolume, and the two-site target using the canonical quartic onsite and quadratic/quartic bond Hamiltonian.
Build the commuting all-bond bilinear kick in the joint coordinate basis and evaluate both signs of delta.
Embed endpoint, one-layer, and full-support shifted-positive Hamiltonian weights into the full tensor product and compute the two-sided form and graph ratios.
Check the q invariance and p one-layer recurrence while retaining the finite truncated-CCR residual; rebuild the full calculation in an independent lane and compile Lean R266 arithmetic fixtures.
finding: Primary 167/167, independent 166/166, and integrated 183/183 with Lean R266 PASS. For (volume,n)=(2,3), (4,3), and (8,2), the maximum finite-CCR residuals are 0.27537395, 0.54958861, and 0.31786266. The maximum endpoint form/graph ratios are (1.08474437,1.04151062), (1.12461836,1.06048025), and approximately (1,1); the one-layer ratios are (1.08474437,1.04151062), (1.15620360,1.07526908), and approximately (1,1).
decision_reason: The finite all-bond and two-orientation support-weight calculation is reproducible, but one-layer support is not monotone-improving on the nontrivial four-site row, the finite CCR residual remains visible, and the full eight-site n=2 row is cutoff-degenerate. The data therefore selects no uniform critical topology and cannot promote the all-bond or direct projected gate.
boundary: Finite exact graph and truncated oscillator rows only; no source-, volume-, cutoff-, beta-, common-core-, thermodynamic-, OS/KMS/GNS-, gap-, continuum-, C6-, Sector-A-, or Pre-A-level conclusion.
next_action: Run a direct projected D,delta-D Cauchy audit on the structured local test class using the nontrivial n=3 face, with the modular/domain residual explicit; if the constants grow, register that scaling obstruction rather than inferring common alpha.
no_overclaim: This is a claim-nonbearing finite diagnostic, not a volume-, source-, cutoff-, or beta-uniform recurrence theorem, a common dynamics, a direct D,delta-D theorem, an OS/KMS/GNS result, a gap, a continuum result, or a C6/Sector-A/Pre-A result.
closed: finite exact graph and all-bond kick construction
finite endpoint/one-layer/full support weight form ratios in both orientations
finite q invariance and p recurrence with explicit truncated-CCR residual
independent numerical reproduction and Lean R266 fixture check
open: exact common-core CCR and modular-domain transfer
direct projected D and delta-D Cauchy, product/core density, and exhaustion
common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, and Pre-A

adversarial_review.check: The full cube row includes all twelve Hamming-one edges and the face row is labeled separately.
Both signs of the commuting kick are evaluated for every edge.
The finite p recurrence retains and reports its truncated-CCR residual.
Weights are shifted and embedded before spectral powers and norm evaluation.
The n=2 full-cube row is not promoted to a uniformity claim.
The independent lane reconstructs the matrices without importing primary code.
R266 proves arithmetic/support fixtures only, not the numerical spectral result.
Common alpha, D,delta-D, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
